architectureQuestionNotResolvedHere.finding: legacy-design-tools' parcelRecordAllowlist.ts explicitly documents these five as SIBLINGS of a representative key (zoningDistrict for the first two, setbackFrontFt for the other three), deliberately given NO independent slate entry, because 'these ... have NO resolveAllowlist call site of their own anywhere in this repo (grep-confirmed) ... A slate entry literally spelled "<county>:setbackSideFt" would never be read by any code.' That is true of LDT's OWN consumers. It is NOT true of hauska-engine's retrieval-api reader (parcel-record-reader.ts readParcelRecord), which iterates every rail key independently with no group/representative-key concept -- it WOULD read and act on a literal '<county>:setbackSideFt' entry. All five pairs read verdict=pass everywhere it matters (side/rear/corner: pass in 5 of 6 counties, excluded only in Hays 48209; zoningJurisdictionKey/zoningProvenance: pass in all 6). Confirmed live for the Bastrop probe parcel: parcel_record_cell holds setbackSideFt=10, setbackRearFt=30, setbackCornerFt=20 (source '@empressaio/setback-corpus@1.1.0:bastrop-development-code', the same ordinance-sourced figures the buildable-envelope endpoint and MCP already serve as 30/10/30/20 -- this lane's own live MCP pull via mcp__claude_ai_Smart_Site__get_smart_site confirms this exactly, see probe artifact). Slating these five would resolve OPS-23 finding F3's setback disagreement for the panel entirely. This lane does NOT recommend simply appending the five entries to both files, because doing so treats a documented, deliberate architectural choice in LDT as inert when it is being read by a second, newer consumer LDT's own comment did not anticipate -- that is a design decision (does the reader need its own representative-key logic instead of literal independent entries?) for whoever owns both the reader and the allowlist, not a call this lane makes unilaterally by editing two files it does not write to.
architectureQuestionNotResolvedHere.requestedAction: A ruling or a dedicated design lane, spanning hauska-engine (parcel-record-reader.ts) and legacy-design-tools (parcelRecordAllowlist.ts), before either file gains a literal '<county>:setbackSideFt'-shaped (or zoning-sibling) entry.

contradicted: The dispatch's 'Factory slate' framing (mission section header, and 'the slate is the factory's per-(county, rail) gate verdict') is imprecise: the GATE VERDICT is factory-owned (parcel_gate_verdict, written by hauska-factory's publish-gate-sched); the SLATE (the code-owned allowlist that actually decides serve state) is legacy-design-tools' parcelRecordAllowlist.ts, vendored into hauska-engine's parcel-record-slate.json -- neither in this lane's registered repos. See F-A.

The dispatch's 'ten rails still riding the atom chain are slated' framing treats all ten as equally independent slate candidates. Five of them (zoningJurisdictionKey, zoningProvenance, setbackSideFt, setbackRearFt, setbackCornerFt) are documented, by the canonical allowlist's own extensive comment, as deliberately-ungated SIBLINGS of a representative key with 'no resolveAllowlist call site of their own' in that repo -- a genuine architecture question, not a plain slate-and-go. See F-B.

Mission item 2's premise ('the panel's dollar rails and owner are gated' as a thing to build) was already false as a gap: live verification found it already true in production on 2026-09-13, before this lane wrote any code (built by P152-PANEL, PR #390). See F-C. Nothing in the dispatch or OPS-23 program doc was wrong about WHY this matters (entitlement-gate risk is real); only about whether it was still open.

Mission item 3's premise ('retire the legacy path by decline') was already mostly built: composeRecordPatch and composeZoningSetbackOverride (P152-RAILS, PR #393) already implement exactly this mechanism generically for nine of the ten rails, activating automatically once slated. See F-D. The one genuinely new finding within item 3's own frame: zoningProvenance has no wire field to retire TO -- a gap this lane found, not one the dispatch or lane 3 named.

'Staging first, then production' (mission item 1) does not apply to the gate evaluation step as written: gate-rail-cli.mjs / publish-gate-sched.mjs read whatever is currently in parcel_record_cell (there is one such table, no staging duplicate for this specific job); the staging-then-production shape in the canon preamble describes the PUBLISH/bake pipeline (bastrop-publish.mjs, staging-reset), a different job family. Confirmed by reading both files in full -- neither references a staging FACTORY_DATABASE_URL variant, and Secret Manager holds exactly one FACTORY_DATABASE_URL secret.
Nothing else in the dispatch, the OPS-23 program doc, or P-152 lane 1/2/3's closes was found wrong.
